successors.name: Roman Republic
successors.text: 'from Leuca in the southeast to Kailia and Egnatia in the northwest, covering most of the Salento peninsula': Lecce, Brindisi and the Taranto hinterland without Taras itself

ledger.x: Mid-6th century BC: the Messapii of Salento.
467 BC: the war with Taras ends.
266 BC: Rome takes the rest of Salento.
266 BC: the independent Messapii end; they 'became Romanised' and 'the language became extinct following the Roman conquest'.

wars.name: Tarentine war against the Iapygians
wars.outcome: Messapian and Peucetian victory over Taras and Rhegion in 473 (470 on the Iapygians page), the war lasting to 467; no border changed.

wars.name: Pyrrhic War
wars.outcome: The Messapii 'sided with Tarentum and Pyrrhus the king of Epirus'; Rome conquered them only afterwards (267-266).

wars.name: Roman conquest of the Salento
wars.outcome: Roman victory: Brundisium and the Messapii taken in 267, the Salento in 266; Brundisium became Rome's port for the East.

certainty.note: The page gives Leuca, Kailia and Egnatia as limits and no boundary with the Peucetians.
